userStories.title: Native ask_human offers choice questions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let native ask_human calls carry parsed structured questions through the session interaction handler without changing legacy text asks or their budget.

**Motivation** — The native `ask_human` tool takes only `{ text }` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/ask-human.ts`), so a model that wants a choice has to write the options into prose.

**Approach** — Native `ask_human` (nax-agent)

`askHumanToolDefinition.inputSchema` gains an optional `questions` array property describing the shape above. Its description says each question takes 2 to 8 options, that `multiSelect` allows several answers, and that the person can always type their own answer. The `text` property stays required: it is the context line above the questions. `NATIVE_CHOICE_MAX_OPTIONS = 8` is exported from `ask-human.ts` (not from the `.` entry).

In `packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-tool-batch.ts` the `ask_human` branch reads `call.input.questions`. When it is present, it runs `parseChoiceQuestions(input.questions, { maxOptions: NATIVE_CHOICE_MAX_OPTIONS, allowOther: true })`. A failed parse answers the call with an error tool result whose content starts `Invalid questions: ` followed by the reason. It spends no interaction budget and makes no interaction call. A successful parse passes the questions to `handleAskHumanCall`, which sends `{ kind: "question", text: renderChoiceQuestionsText(question, questions), prompt: question, questions }`. The tool result content is the answer text, which for a choice answer is the `formatChoiceAnswers` output.

Session surface consumed by this story:

- `AdapterInteraction`, the `InteractionHandler` request type (`packages/nax-agent/src/session/interaction-handler.ts`). Baseline: `{ kind: "question"; text: string }`. Target: `{ kind: "question"; text: string; prompt?: string; questions?: readonly ChoiceQuestion[] }`. For a choice ask, `text` is already `renderChoiceQuestionsText(prompt, questions)`, so a handler that reads only `text` (`packages/nax/src/agents/run-interaction-handler.ts`) shows the options unchanged.
- `answerQuestion` in `packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts` calls `deps.asks.askChoices(prompt, questions)` when the request has `questions` and the port has `askChoices`, and answers with the result's `text`. Otherwise it keeps today's `askQuestion(text)` call. That call already carries the rendered options.

Shared parser contract supplied by US-001: `parseChoiceQuestions` accepts an array of 1 to `CHOICE_MAX_QUESTIONS` objects, each with a non-empty string `question`, a string `header` (cut to `CHOICE_HEADER_MAX_CHARS` characters; an empty or missing header becomes `Q<n>`, 1-based), an `options` array of 2 to `limits.maxOptions` objects each with a non-empty string `label` and an optional string `description`, and an optional boolean `multiSelect` (default `false`). `allowOther` is copied from `limits.allowOther` and `required` is `true`. Option labels must be unique within one question (case-insensitive). Any other shape returns `{ ok: false, reason }`. The reason names the first failing path, for example `questions[1].options: expected 2-8 options, got 1`.

Failure handling:
- Native `ask_human` `questions` fails `parseChoiceQuestions`: error tool result `Invalid questions: <reason>`; no budget spent; no interaction call.
- Embedder answers a choice ask with a plain `{ text }`: resolves to `{ text }` with no `answers`; native passes the text to the model.
- Choice ask times out, is cancelled, or the turn ends: `askChoices` resolves `null`; native answers "No human operator is available..." as today.
- Ask port without `askChoices`: native: `askQuestion` with the rendered text.

**Scope** — In: native schema/option limit, parse-before-dispatch, optional questions on handleAskHumanCall and AdapterInteraction, session handler preference/fallback, scripted-turn seam tests. Out: shared contract/pending-table implementation (US-001), ACP form translation (US-003), pure reducer (US-004), chat layout/controller (US-005). The nax run-time ACP ask port (`packages/nax/src/agents/acp/ask-port.ts`), `run-interaction-handler.ts` and the Telegram/webhook interaction plugins do not implement `askChoices`; they keep the text path, which carries the rendered options. No new config key: the choice card is always on in chat, and `ask_human`'s budget (`ASK_HUMAN_BUDGET`) is unchanged.

**Interface** — Target request and consumed signatures:
```ts
{ kind: "question"; text: string; prompt?: string; questions?: readonly ChoiceQuestion[] }
parseChoiceQuestions(
  input: unknown,
  limits: { readonly maxOptions: number; readonly allowOther: boolean },
): { readonly ok: true; readonly questions: readonly ChoiceQuestion[] } | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: string };
askChoices?(prompt: string, questions: readonly ChoiceQuestion[], opts?: { readonly signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<ChoiceAskResult | null>
```

Implementation/test notes: modify src/native/session/ask-human.ts, turn-tool-batch.ts and turn-ask-human.ts plus src/session/interaction-handler.ts and session-interaction.ts. Add test/unit/native/session/ask-human-choices.test.ts following test/unit/native/session/turn-loop-seam.test.ts (scripted ask_human) and test/unit/native/session-adapter-abort-reasons.test.ts (createSessionInteractionHandler with a fake asks). Its seam AC drives a scripted native turn whose model calls `ask_human` with `questions`, through `createSessionInteractionHandler` with a fake `asks`, and asserts `askChoices` received them. Keep no-questions requests exactly `{ kind: "question", text }`, preserve synthetic result bypass of ordinary tool hooks, and do not add the native limit to the public entry. Null answers retain the exact existing tool error content: `No human operator is available for this run. Proceed on your best judgement.`
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] askHumanToolDefinition.inputSchema.properties has a questions property of type array, and required is still exactly ["text"].

[unit] handleAskHumanCall with questions calls the interaction handler once with { kind: "question", text: renderChoiceQuestionsText(question, questions), prompt: question, questions }, and returns a tool result whose content is the handler's answer.
[unit] handleAskHumanCall without questions calls the interaction handler with { kind: "question", text } and no questions or prompt key, as before.

Its model calls ask_human with { text: "Pick", questions: [one question with 3 options] }. askChoices is called with "Pick" and one parsed ChoiceQuestion, and the tool result the model receives next is the text askChoices resolved to.

[unit] In the same harness, a model call of ask_human with a questions entry holding one option gets an error tool result whose content starts with 'Invalid questions: '. askChoices is not called, and a second valid ask_human call in the same turn is still answered (the budget was not spent).

[unit] When a native choice ask times out, is cancelled, or its turn ends and askChoices resolves null, its tool result content is 'No human operator is available for this run. Proceed on your best judgement.', as today.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module native tool dispatch, session interaction routing and budget preservation require a real scripted-turn seam; session-code involvement applies the strict three-session override.

userStories.title: Choice card state model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a pure immutable reducer for single/multi choice selection, inline Other editing, question tabs and submission review.

**Motivation** — Agent questions do not, and nothing supports multi-select, an Other row or several questions in one ask.

**Approach** — New pure model `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/choice-question.ts`:
- `ChoiceKey`, a normalised key:
  `{ kind: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" | "return" | "escape" | "space" | "backspace" } | { kind: "char"; char: string }`.
- `initialChoiceState(questions)`.
- `reduceChoiceKey(state, questions, key) -> { state, outcome?: { kind: "submit"; answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[] } | { kind: "decline" } }`.

The state is `{ tab, cursor, selected: number[][], other: (string | undefined)[], editing: boolean, draft: string, review: boolean }`. It is immutable: every key returns a new state. The reducer is split into one helper per key class so `check:complexity` stays green.

Key map of the choice card (the cursor rows are the options plus, when `allowOther`, a last `Other...` row):

| Key | Single-select question | Multi-select question |
|:---|:---|:---|
| up / down | move cursor, clamped at the ends | same |
| digit `1`-`9` naming an option | select that option and advance | toggle that option |
| digit beyond the option count | ignored | ignored |
| space | select the cursor option (no advance) | toggle the cursor option |
| enter on an option | select it and advance | advance |
| enter or space on `Other...` | start editing (inline text box) | same |
| left / right | previous / next tab (only with 2+ questions) | same |
| esc | decline the ask | same |

- "Advance" means the next tab. From the last question with 2+ questions it opens the review step. With one question it submits, provided the question is answered or not required.
- Selecting a single-select option clears that question's `other`.
- While editing, digit and space keys are typed characters. Typing edits `draft`. Enter with a non-empty trimmed draft stores it as that question's `other`, clears a single-select's selected option, and advances. Esc leaves editing without changing `other`.
- On a required question with nothing selected and no `other`, the advancing keys stay on the question.
- Starting to edit a question that already has an `other` seeds `draft` with it. Changing tab puts the cursor on the first selected option of the new tab, else on row 0.
- The review step lists each question's header with its `formatChoiceAnswers` line. Enter submits when every required question is answered; otherwise it moves to the first unanswered required tab. Left goes back to the last tab.
- Shift-tab and tab are not bound by the card: shift-tab stays `cycleMode` in `useChatKeys`.

**Scope** — In: pure ChoiceKey/state/initialization/reduction, option index ordering, editing, clamping, advancement, review and outcomes. Out: ask-card.ts model kind, AskCard.tsx, Ink key normalization, layout, controller and component wiring (US-005); contract validation/formatters (US-001); native tool producer (US-002); ACP producer (US-003). Mouse clicks on choice options are not handled.

**Interface** — Verbatim normalized key, reducer and state declarations from the design:
```ts
{ kind: "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" | "return" | "escape" | "space" | "backspace" } | { kind: "char"; char: string }
initialChoiceState(questions)
reduceChoiceKey(state, questions, key) -> { state, outcome?: { kind: "submit"; answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[] } | { kind: "decline" } }
{ tab, cursor, selected: number[][], other: (string | undefined)[], editing: boolean, draft: string, review: boolean }
```

Implementation/test notes: this story only adds src/tui/chat/choice-question.ts and test/unit/tui/chat/choice-question.test.ts. Do not edit ask-card.ts or AskCard.tsx. Use the shared public ChoiceQuestion/ChoiceAnswer types. Keep selected indexes ascending/unique and Other out of selected. Test reducer calls directly, including ignored keys returning a new state with equal values and unchanged input. Apply the required-answer advance guard to the resulting answer: single-select down then Return selects index 1 before advancing, while Return that leaves a required question unanswered does not advance. No React, Ink, session port, timers or I/O belong in this module.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] initialChoiceState(questions) has tab 0, cursor 0, an empty selection per question, editing false and review false.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a single-select question with keys down then return selects option index 1. With one question, it returns outcome { kind: "submit", answers: [{ selected: [1] }] }.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a single-select question with { kind: "char", char: "3" } selects index 2 and advances. A digit beyond the option count leaves the state equal to the input.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey clamps the cursor: up at row 0 stays 0, and down at the last row (the Other... row when allowOther) stays there.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a multi-select question: space on row 0 and char 3 give selection [0, 2]; a second space on row 0 gives [2]; no outcome is returned.

[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a required question with nothing selected and no other (use a multi-select question, whose Return key advances without selecting): return stays on the same tab with no outcome.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a non-required multi-select question with nothing selected: return advances (with one question it submits { selected: [] }).

[unit] reduceChoiceKey return on the Other... row sets editing true. Char keys (including a digit and space) build draft, backspace removes the last character, and return with draft deno stores other deno and advances. For single-select it clears that question's selected index.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey on a single-select question whose other is set: selecting an option clears other.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey while editing: return with a whitespace-only draft stays editing, and escape leaves editing with other unchanged and no decline outcome.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey with escape when not editing returns outcome { kind: "decline" }.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey with two questions: right moves to tab 1, left moves back to tab 0, and right on the last tab stays there.
[unit] reduceChoiceKey with two questions: answering the last question opens the review step (review true) with no outcome.
[unit] In the review step, return with every required question answered returns outcome submit with one answer per question in question order.
[unit] In the review step, return with required question 0 unanswered leaves review and sets tab 0.
[unit] In the review step, left leaves review and sets tab to the last question.

[unit] reduceChoiceKey space on the Other... row of a multi-select question sets editing true and leaves selected unchanged, so no state ever holds a selected index greater than or equal to the question's option count.
[unit] Every reduceChoiceKey call returns a new state object and leaves the input state unchanged.
[unit] With one question, reduceChoiceKey never sets review true: the advancing key submits directly.

routing.reasoning: A deterministic pure reducer and its mirrored tests implement a fully specified key/state machine without I/O, session lifecycle changes or integration wiring.

userStories.title: Choice card model kind, drawing and chat wiring
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render structured session questions as budgeted interactive choice cards and submit their original-label answers through the chat controller.

**Motivation** — The chat question card (`AskCardQuestion` in `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ask-card.ts`) is only a text box.

**Approach** — Chat (nax), drawing and wiring:

- `askCardModel` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ask-card.ts`). Target: a `question` ask that carries `questions` becomes a new model kind `AskCardChoiceQuestion { kind: "choice-question"; title; prompt; border; questions }`, with every string passed through `sanitizeText`. A `question` ask without `questions` keeps `AskCardQuestion`.
- New component `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChoiceQuestionCard.tsx` draws the model, holds the `ChoiceState` locally (as `AskCard` holds its selection today) and maps ink's `(input, key)` to `ChoiceKey`. `choiceQuestionLayout(model, state, { width, budget, theme, expiresAt, nowMs })` is the single place its rows are decided. `AskCard.tsx` is already 659 lines, so the new card's rows, keys and rendering live in the new files, and `AskCard`, `askCardLayout` and `measureAskCard` only delegate the `choice-question` kind.
- Measurement is state-independent, because `measureFrameSurfaces` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/frame-surfaces.ts`) measures without the card's state. `measureAskCard` for a `choice-question` returns:
  - `desired`: the largest row count `choiceQuestionLayout` draws with an unlimited budget, over every tab and the review step;
  - `minimum`: the rows of the frame rules, the title, the tab strip (when shown), one question line, one option row, both `(n more ...)` rows, the hint row and the countdown row.

  `choiceQuestionLayout` never draws more rows than its budget. At a budget below `desired`, the prompt and the question are each cut to one row ending in `...` before any option row is withheld.
- Result mapping: `askCardLayout` returns the choice card's rows as `head` (rules, title, tab strip, prompt, question), `rows` (option window and `Other...`), `tail` (hint, countdown, bottom rule), no `input` (`inputMaxRows` 0), and `elided` as the count of option rows the window withholds. `measureAskCard` returns `elided` 0 and `marker` 0 at `desired`, because the window's `(n more ...)` rows stand in for an elision marker.
- `ChatAskController` (`packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts`) gains `answerChoices(requestId: string, answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[], text: string): void`, which calls `options.answer(requestId, { text, answers })` for an open session `question` and removes it. The `text` argument is `formatChoiceAnswers` over the event's original (unsanitised) `questions`, so the agent reads its own labels back. The card catches an `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_ANSWER` throw, logs it at warn, and keeps the card open. On a `decline` outcome the card calls its `onDismiss` prop, which is the path the text card's escape takes today (`ChatApp`'s `dismissQuestion`: two-press escape confirm, `declineQuestion`, turn cancel).

Drawing:
- the tab strip `[Header] [Header] [Submit]`, shown only with 2+ questions (the active tab is bold, answered tabs use the success colour);
- the prompt (when non-empty) and the question line;
- one row per option: `> ` on the cursor row, `[x] ` / `[ ] ` for multi or `(*) ` / `( ) ` for single, then `n. label`, then the description in the muted colour, cut to the width;
- the `Other...` row, which shows the stored other text when set;
- a hint row naming the keys for the current question kind;
- the existing countdown row.

Long lists: when the option rows do not fit the budget, the card draws a window of option rows that keeps the cursor visible, plus `(n more above)` / `(n more below)` rows. Those rows count against the budget. The question line, the hint row and the countdown are never withheld.

Reducer behavior consumed from US-004:
- "Advance" means the next tab. From the last question with 2+ questions it opens the review step. With one question it submits, provided the question is answered or not required.
- Selecting a single-select option clears that question's `other`.
- While editing, digit and space keys are typed characters. Typing edits `draft`. Enter with a non-empty trimmed draft stores it as that question's `other`, clears a single-select's selected option, and advances. Esc leaves editing without changing `other`.
- On a required question with nothing selected and no `other`, the advancing keys stay on the question.
- Starting to edit a question that already has an `other` seeds `draft` with it. Changing tab puts the cursor on the first selected option of the new tab, else on row 0.
- The review step lists each question's header with its `formatChoiceAnswers` line. Enter submits when every required question is answered; otherwise it moves to the first unanswered required tab. Left goes back to the last tab.
- Shift-tab and tab are not bound by the card: shift-tab stays `cycleMode` in `useChatKeys`.

**Scope** — In: sanitized model kind, separate card component and centralized layout, state-independent measurement/delegates, Ink key normalization/inline editor, controller answerChoices, original-label formatting, warn-and-retain validation failures, onDismiss reuse and existing fake compatibility updates. Out: changing pure reducer behavior (US-004), shared pending/session contract (US-001), native tool producer (US-002), ACP form producer (US-003). Run asks (`packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/run-asks.ts`) and the host-choice card (`AskCardChoice`) keep their current cards; they are not moved onto the choice card. Mouse clicks on choice options are not handled. No new config key: the choice card is always on in chat, and `ask_human`'s budget (`ASK_HUMAN_BUDGET`) is unchanged.

**Interface** — Verbatim target model, layout/controller signatures and reducer consumption:
```ts
AskCardChoiceQuestion { kind: "choice-question"; title; prompt; border; questions }
choiceQuestionLayout(model, state, { width, budget, theme, expiresAt, nowMs })
answerChoices(requestId: string, answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[], text: string): void
reduceChoiceKey(state, questions, key) -> { state, outcome?: { kind: "submit"; answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[] } | { kind: "decline" } }
export function formatChoiceAnswers(questions: readonly ChoiceQuestion[], answers: readonly ChoiceAnswer[]): string;
```

Implementation/test notes: create src/tui/chat/ChoiceQuestionCard.tsx, test/unit/tui/chat/choice-question-layout.test.ts and test/ui/chat/choice-question-card.test.tsx. Keep new layout/key helpers in new files if required by file/complexity limits and include their tests in this story, never grow AskCard.tsx with the new implementation. Existing AskCardLayout.rows is a numeric total-height contract; adapt the choice layout's option-window rows at delegation while retaining correct total height for frame consumers and legacy cards. Existing frame-surfaces has no choice state and must stay able to measure desired across every tab/review. Keep measurement stable across selection/editing; layout must not exceed budget, and do not steal question/hint/countdown rows for window markers. Render all text via existing display-width-aware StyledLine utilities. Choice inline editing is local to this card; generic askCardLayout input and inputMaxRows stay 0.

Submission seam: render `AskCard` for a pending question, send the keys, and assert the session `answer` callback got `{ text, answers }`. Format with original event questions, not the sanitized display copy. Call options.answer before removing the ask so a thrown validation error leaves it pending; catch AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_ANSWER in the card and warn without throwing out of render/input. Ensure the delegated card is the only key owner, using latest-state refs for batched Ink keys. Bare Escape calls onDismiss once; ChatApp owns confirmation/decline/turn cancellation. Preserve text-box question behavior.

Modify required existing fakes, keeping every existing assertion: packages/nax/test/ui/chat/ask-card.test.tsx (typed ChatAskController stub); chat-app.test.tsx, chat-app-mentions.test.tsx and slash-commands.test.tsx (typed ChatHost['asks'] literals gain `answerChoices: () => {}`). Add controller cases to packages/nax/test/unit/chat/ask-controller.test.ts. Follow test/ui/chat/chat-asks-keys.test.tsx and the existing HOST-choice test/ui/chat/choice-card.test.tsx for Ink key driving; do not repurpose or remove that separate card's assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] askCardModel for a question ask carrying questions returns kind: "choice-question" with the questions' strings sanitised (an ESC byte in an option label is removed).
[unit] askCardModel for a question ask without questions returns kind: "question" as before.
[unit] choiceQuestionLayout for a two-question model draws a tab strip row naming both headers and Submit. For a one-question model it draws no tab strip.
[unit] choiceQuestionLayout draws the cursor option row with '> ', multi-select rows with '[x] ' / '[ ] ', and single-select rows with '(*) ' / '( ) ', followed by n. label.
[unit] choiceQuestionLayout draws an option's description after its label in the muted colour, cut so the row fits width.
[unit] choiceQuestionLayout draws a last Other... row when allowOther is true, which shows the stored other text when one is set, and no such row when allowOther is false.

[unit] choiceQuestionLayout with 12 options and a budget 6 rows short of the unlimited draw draws a window that contains the cursor row plus a (n more below) row at cursor 0, and a (n more above) row when the cursor is on the last option. The total row count never exceeds the budget.

[unit] choiceQuestionLayout at a budget equal to measureAskCard(...).minimum still draws the question line, one option row, the hint row and the countdown row. With a 300-character question at width 40, the question is drawn as one row ending in ... and the row count does not exceed the budget.
[unit] choiceQuestionLayout draws a review step listing each question's header with its formatChoiceAnswers line when the state's review is true.
[unit] measureAskCard for a two-question choice-question model returns a desired equal to the largest row count choiceQuestionLayout draws with an unlimited budget over both tabs and the review step.
[unit] ChatAskController.answerChoices(requestId, answers, text) on an open session question calls the answer option with { text, answers } and removes the ask from pending().
[unit] ChatAskController.answerChoices on an unknown request id, or on a host question (host-question- id), does not call answer.

[integration] Rendering AskCard for a pending session question with one single-select question and sending down then return calls the controller's answer callback once with answers: [{ selected: [1] }] and text equal to formatChoiceAnswers(questions, answers).
[integration] Rendering AskCard for a pending session question with one multi-select question and sending space, down, space, return answers with answers: [{ selected: [0, 1] }].

[integration] Rendering AskCard for a pending session choice question whose answer callback throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_ANSWER keeps the choice card drawn after the submitting key, and the render does not throw.
[integration] Rendering AskCard for a pending session choice question and sending escape calls the onDismiss prop once, and the answer callback is not called.
[integration] Rendering AskCard for a pending session question without questions still draws the text-box question card and submits typed text through answerQuestion.

analysis:
Repository discovery: the codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this tool set, so findings below come from direct reads and regex text searches in the supplied execution repository. This is an additive enhancement across three existing TypeScript packages, not greenfield. No implementation or test commands were run while drafting or auditing this PRD.

Refine audit: enumerated every explicit spec AC and compared it, including its trailing regression qualifiers, against the same story's acceptanceCriteria. The one-to-one ordinal inventory is US-001 spec AC01-20 -> PRD AC01-20; US-002 AC01-08 -> AC01-08; US-003 AC01-16 -> AC01-16; US-004 AC01-19 -> AC01-19; US-005 AC01-17 -> AC01-17 (80 original ACs total, none removed or reassigned). The four additional mandatory ACs already in the draft enumerate the spec's failure table: cancellation/turn-end null in US-001, native plain reply and null-to-no-operator mapping in US-002, ACP cancellation mapping in US-003. All assertions are observable via return values, emitted/captured requests, exceptions, public import/type usage, rendered lines or reducer/controller state. Every story already has negative criteria; legacy regression anchors remain in US-001's validator-free text replies, US-002's unchanged plain requests and unspent invalid-call budget, US-003's existing reply matching and per-field fallback, and US-005's unchanged text card. US-004 is additive and protects ignored-key values and input immutability. All seven feature-level outOfScope items and all five binding dependency/workdir assignments are preserved. No story-local deferral has been hoisted. Corrected the fallback instruction's double punctuation and clarified that the required-unanswered Return fixture is multi-select: its key advances without selecting, unlike the single-select Enter action which selects before the advance guard. This retains both original reducer assertions. Restored the spec-recommended chat-asks-keys.test.tsx to US-005 contextFiles in place of ask-card.ts; ask-card.ts remains an explicitly in-scope source edit. US-002 lists five of its six recommended context files and names the remaining abort-reasons fake-handler harness in its description. Simplified US-003's unnecessarily mandatory transport harness to the real exported answerElicitation handler with typed fake asks (the existing test pattern and production backend.ts:199 call site), removed auxiliary context entries, and lowered its complexity to medium while retaining the explicit session-code three-session strategy override. The existing shown helper requires shown(text, ctx.secrets), clarified alongside the design's shorthand. No new helper, dependency, backend routing change or production transport is required for that story.

Architecture and implementation order: US-001 establishes the public nax-agent contract and session settlement behavior; US-002 and US-003 independently produce structured asks through that contract; US-004 supplies the pure chat reducer; US-005 integrates rendering and submission. Preserve exactly the declared dependencies: US-002/003/004 depend on US-001, US-005 depends on US-004 (and therefore transitively on US-001). US-005 must not depend on the native or ACP producer stories. nax-agent-acp imports shared types/functions only from @nathapp/nax-agent's public entry, never internal/deep paths. nax imports the ACP package only through /client; no nax-ai changes are needed. docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:141 documents the dependency graph, and :154 documents source/function limits. nax-agent and nax-agent-acp shipped code remains Node-compatible, while nax uses its existing Bun/React/Ink stack. Follow package-local aliases/import conventions and named public exports.

US-001 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-types.ts:181 defines the existing question event with requestId/text/expiresAt/answerable and :218 defines AnswerReply as decision-or-text; add optional questions/prompt only for choice events and optional answers on the text branch. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-backend.ts:53 defines SessionAskPort; askQuestion's optional signal at :65 must be mirrored by optional askChoices so existing backend/embedder fakes remain compatible. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-ask-port.ts:29 builds the port and :62 implements askQuestion: no-turn returns null, caller signal is combined with the running turn signal, the pending request is emitted, and only a human text settlement returns text. Reuse those lifecycle semantics for askChoices; always emit rendered options in text so consumers ignoring structured metadata do not lose choices. packages/nax-agent/src/session/pending-asks.ts:24 exposes the table, :35 stores entry state, :59 issues requests/timers/abort listeners, and :80 answers. Currently kind validation happens before pending-state handling (:92); insert the optional validator inside the pending branch after the kind check, before finish. Throwing for an invalid structured reply must neither clear its timer nor settle/delete its pending request; expired/cancelled requests must not invoke its validator. Keep close/cancelAll/late-status behavior unchanged. packages/nax-agent/src/index.ts:600 is the actual end of the 600-line entry; consolidate named re-exports without removing existing names, introducing star exports, or increasing the cap. Regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt with bun run api:update from packages/nax-agent; never hand-edit the snapshot or bump versions.

US-001 tests: packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/session-ask-port.test.ts:8 already builds a real port/table with a controlled running-turn closure and :67 tests text settlement/cancel; :80 covers extra signals. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/session/pending-asks.test.ts:17 provides manual timers through _agentSessionDeps and :48 starts the table behavior suite; :70 tests expiry, :79 cancellation, :101 malformed/kind mismatch. Extend these existing tests for the new session behavior and create test/unit/session/choice-questions.test.ts for the pure contract and package-entry imports. Additional consumers found by search include native-backend.test.ts, session-interaction.test.ts, session-interaction-cancel-grace.test.ts and session-ask-link.test.ts; optional methods and additive reply fields should keep those working. A regression test must be demonstrated failing against old behavior before implementation.

US-002 findings: packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/ask-human.ts:18 advertises the tool with only required text (:24-25); add optional questions and module-only NATIVE_CHOICE_MAX_OPTIONS=8. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-loop.ts:275 advertises askHumanToolDefinition only when maxInteractions is positive. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-tool-batch.ts:145 handles ask_human before ordinary tool hooks, constructs its question and calls handleAskHumanCall, incrementing recorded budget only when outcome.exchange exists. Parse questions in this branch before calling the handler or recording exchanges; invalid input must produce one synthetic error result and continue the batch without consuming budget or invoking interaction/ordinary tool hooks. packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/turn-ask-human.ts:19 defines handleAskHumanCall, :32 checks the existing exchange budget, :42 sends the question request, :48 maps null to the exact existing no-operator error string, and :58 records a real exchange. Add the optional parsed questions while preserving the exact no-questions request shape (no undefined metadata keys). packages/nax-agent/src/session/interaction-handler.ts:4 defines AdapterInteraction's question branch. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts:334 defines answerQuestion, :335 currently calls askQuestion(text), and :341 dispatches the request; change the helper to receive the question request and prefer askChoices only when both questions and the optional method exist. Return its text, not a new response type, preserving InteractionExchange and tool-result contracts. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:31 defines ASK_HUMAN_BUDGET=10 and :173 passes it as maxInteractions; neither changes.

US-002 tests and seam: packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session/turn-loop-seam.test.ts:76 builds SendTurnOpts and :98 drives runNativeTurn with a scripted complete function, transcript store and hook counter; :99-145 already pins ask_human budget/after_tool bypass behavior. Mirror its harness in the new ask-human-choices.test.ts rather than altering existing no-questions assertions. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session-adapter-abort-reasons.test.ts:21-30 imports the real session interaction/ask-port components and :113 captures timer callbacks without wall-clock waits. New scripted turns must run through createSessionInteractionHandler with fake asks and observe the next model-visible tool result, not just inspect helper inputs. Confirm an invalid first questions payload leaves a later valid call in the same turn answerable.

US-003 findings: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/elicitation.ts is currently 256 lines. Choice at :47 and Field at :53 retain original values separately from displayed labels. shown() at :71 strips controls/invisibles, scrubs secrets and caps bytes. choicesOf() at :92 accepts up to MAX_CHOICES=32 (not the native limit of 8), and withCompanions() at :121 folds *_custom fields before parseForm() (:133) returns. Add the select-only choice branch to askFields() (:224) AFTER folding; do not run the native parser over ACP fields, since ACP can have a single option, more than eight options, required=false, and different allowOther rules. questionText() (:167) joins title and description with ': '; reuse the same joining semantics without repeating the prompt per field. ownAnswerHint() (:153) encodes the required-single/required-multi companion distinction. applyReply() (:212) already provides the plain-text single-field fallback. ask() (:219) enforces pre-abort cancellation, sanitization, signal forwarding and rejection-to-null; the new askChoices path must do the same for each displayed string, while mapping selected indexes back to ORIGINAL choice.value and original field/companion keys. A companion alone is not enough for a required multi: decline with REQUIRED_NOTE. A missing structured answer for multiple fields declines with NO_MATCH_NOTE. Preserve profile gating at answerElicitation() (:244-256); do not modify permissions or mixed/large-form behavior. packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/backend.ts:199 wires answerElicitation into the inbound handler using the binding's signal.

US-003 tests: packages/nax-agent-acp/test/unit/client/elicitation.test.ts:16 builds a typed fake SessionAskPort WITHOUT askChoices, :34 constructs the context, :39 builds wire-form requests, and :54 supplies Claude's real-style single-select/companion fixture. Its existing suites (:78, :152, :217, :260, :302) anchor text matching, required companions, sanitation and cancellation. Keep their assertions intact. Create elicitation-choices.test.ts exercising the exported answerElicitation handler with typed fake SessionAskPort objects, as existing tests do, rather than only an isolated mapping helper. backend.ts:199 confirms this is the production elicitation/create handler, so direct handler tests exercise the specified seam without requiring a new ACP transport harness or backend edits. A fake transport is optional if useful; never launch a real CLI adapter.

US-004 findings: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ask-card.ts:85 defines the text-only question model, :92 the separate host-choice model, :100 the union, and :195 selects models. Do not modify these in US-004. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/AskCard.tsx:515 shows option key normalization, :556 stores a latestSelected ref because Ink can deliver several keys before React rerenders, and :599 handles host choice independently of approvals. Build a pure immutable choice reducer in a new module without Ink, React, timers or controller dependencies; selected indexes must remain sorted and the synthetic Other row must never become an option index. Guard advancement using the answer after the key's action; an unanswered required multi cannot advance, whereas single-select down+Enter must select and submit exactly as the explicit AC requires. Keep the stated empty-required advance and single-select selection ACs authoritative rather than treating Enter as an unconditional advance. Editing consumes digits/spaces as text and Escape cancels editing without declining; outside editing Escape declines. Left/right change question tabs only, last-question advancement enters review only for multiple questions. The initial selections are empty; no default answer is silently committed.

US-005 findings: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ask-card.ts:195 currently sanitizes question text and returns kind='question'; add a distinct choice-question model preserving order and booleans and sanitize header/question/labels/descriptions/prompt. Keep original event questions untouched for model-facing answer formatting. packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:6 derives ChatPendingAsk from SessionEvent (metadata additions therefore flow through automatically), :67 defines ChatAskController, :233 handles events, :259 returns pending, :290 answers text questions, and :300 declines them. answerChoices must only target open session questions, ignore unknown/host ids, call options.answer BEFORE remove, and let a validation throw leave the ask open. The new card catches AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_ANSWER, logs at warn using existing chat logger conventions (see packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-jobs.ts:83), and remains mounted. Native and ACP labels may contain sanitized-away bytes; formatChoiceAnswers must receive the event's original questions, never the display model.

Layout and rendering integration: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/AskCard.tsx is already 659 lines; :434 defines askCardLayout, :473 measureAskCard and :535 the component. New rows/key handling/rendering belong in new files, with narrow delegates added here; avoid further expanding the existing file. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/frame-surfaces.ts:20 measures before allocation and :29 calls measureAskCard WITHOUT choice state. Desired height must be computed across all question tabs and review, not from the current cursor or tab. Unlimited and constrained draws must share choiceQuestionLayout. Under pressure collapse prompt/question to one ellipsized row before withholding option rows; budget the above/below markers and keep cursor visible. The spec calls the option window 'rows'; note that the current AskCardLayout.rows at AskCard.tsx:161 is a NUMBER used for total height, not an array. Adapt the new layout's option-row collection at the delegation boundary without silently replacing the existing total-height meaning for legacy cards/consumers. Keep input/inputMaxRows zero for choices and account for the option window when computing total rows. At desired, measurement's elided/marker must be zero; the choice window owns its own above/below markers. Below the measured minimum the allocator already chooses a diagnostic (:468-472); do not let the new layout overflow its explicit budget. Row layout must use display-width-aware existing StyledLine helpers, not string-length-only width arithmetic. Inline Other editing is rendered within the new card; the generic text-card input does not replace choice rows.

Keyboard/controller integration and regression risks: AskCard's parent useInput must be inactive for the delegated choice-question kind to prevent double handling; retain the latest-state-ref pattern for burst keys. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/useChatKeys.ts:182-192 reserves shift-tab for cycleMode; new card must not bind tab or shift-tab or turn control/meta chords into selections. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:1310-1315 implements dismissQuestion: session asks during controllable running turns use two-press Escape confirmation, declineQuestion first, then host.cancel. Delegate choice decline to the same onDismiss callback; never directly deny approval/cancel turn inside the new card. Existing host-choice/run asks remain separate.

US-005 tests and fake compatibility: packages/nax/test/ui/chat/choice-card.test.tsx:12-72 is the existing HOST choice-card suite (not a new agent-choice suite); preserve it and mirror its render/act/controller pattern in choice-question-card.test.tsx. packages/nax/test/ui/chat/chat-asks-keys.test.tsx:33-108 mounts ChatApp with a real controller and mock host for keyboard/cancel integration. Add pure layout tests in test/unit/tui/chat/choice-question-layout.test.ts and controller behavior to test/unit/chat/ask-controller.test.ts. Required typed fake updates are test/ui/chat/ask-card.test.tsx:120, chat-app.test.tsx:54, chat-app-mentions.test.tsx:89 and slash-commands.test.tsx:57: add answerChoices stubs without changing old assertions. Existing fakes built by createChatAskController inherit the method automatically.

Migration and constraints: there is no persisted-data migration, new configuration, new dependency, budget increase or release bump. Optional askChoices plus rendered event/request text is the compatibility bridge: old embedders, koda, nax runtime ask ports, interaction plugins and the ACP server continue reading/answering text. Plain text replies to choice asks must not be rejected merely for omitting answers. Native malformed questions are rejected before interaction budget; structured invalid human answers are rejected while preserving the pending request; deadlines/abort/turn end settle null and do not hang close. Public exported types/constants/functions require the generated nax-agent API snapshot. The spec's Creates list is authoritative for new files; its Modifies/None notes are not an exhaustive implementation-file list (native and ACP source edits are still required by the design). All stories write behavior tests as part of implementation, not separate test-only stories. Session settlement/routing stories use the requested strict three-session security/session strategy; the pure reducer has no session/security behavior and uses ordinary TDD. Run targeted Bun tests from the relevant package, never bare bun test; use existing _deps timers and fake adapters, demonstrate regressions fail against old code, and let the workflow's package gates check build/types/lint/API/size. Do not run coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1.
outOfScope: Run asks (`packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/run-asks.ts`) and the host-choice card (`AskCardChoice`) keep their current cards; they are not moved onto the choice card.

The nax-agent ACP server (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/questions.ts`) forwards a choice ask to its ACP client as today's text question built from the event's rendered `text`; mapping `questions` to an ACP elicitation form for that client is not part of this feature.

The nax run-time ACP ask port (`packages/nax/src/agents/acp/ask-port.ts`), `run-interaction-handler.ts` and the Telegram/webhook interaction plugins do not implement `askChoices`; they keep the text path, which carries the rendered options.
Elicitation forms that mix text fields with select fields, or carry more than four select fields, keep the existing one-field-at-a-time text path.
No new config key: the choice card is always on in chat, and `ask_human`'s budget (`ASK_HUMAN_BUDGET`) is unchanged.
Mouse clicks on choice options are not handled.
koda does not render choice questions in this feature; koda's existing `{ text }` reply to a `question` event keeps working.
